terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.summary: The rules for discovering events, buying tickets, listing services and working with HIT KENYA. These terms explain the responsibilities of everyone using the platform.
sections: About HIT KENYA and these terms

HIT KENYA (Events. Experiences. Culture.) is operated by [LEGAL ENTITY NAME], of [ADDRESS], Kenya. These terms govern use of the website, ticketing and listing features and related services when available. Read the Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy and Refund Policy alongside these terms. Any event-specific conditions must be disclosed before purchase and cannot override mandatory consumer protections.

By accepting these terms when registering or entering a transaction, you agree to the applicable conditions. Browsing the website does not waive your statutory rights.
Eligibility and age requirements

You must be at least 18 years old to independently register an account, enter a contract, sell tickets or list services. A parent or lawful guardian must handle purchases or registration for a minor where permitted. Age-restricted events may impose additional entry rules. You must have authority to act for any organisation you represent.
Accounts and security

Provide accurate, current information, protect your credentials and promptly report suspected unauthorised access. Do not share accounts, impersonate others or bypass verification. HIT KENYA may request proportionate verification through an approved secure process before granting organiser or dealer privileges. Registration requests are not automatic approval. Do not send identity documents or face photographs through ordinary WhatsApp enquiries.
Roles on the platform

Organisers and attendees

Organisers create and manage approved events, prices, availability, venue information, RSVP rules and ticket conditions. Attendees purchase tickets, follow venue rules and protect ticket QR codes.

Marketplace and community partners

Vendors, influencers, tour coordinators, venue owners, car hire operators, accommodation providers and other partners are responsible for their offers, qualifications, service quality and contractual obligations. Sponsored content must be identifiable as advertising. Listing approval is not a guarantee of service quality or endorsement.
Listings and permitted use

Provide truthful descriptions, dates, venue and map details, prices, capacity and relevant restrictions. Use only content you are authorised to publish. Update listings promptly when circumstances change. Do not advertise illegal services, fraudulent tickets, misleading claims, counterfeit goods or offerings you cannot fulfil. HIT KENYA may request corrections or remove listings where reasonably necessary.
Prohibited conduct

Do not harass, discriminate, threaten, defraud, spam, impersonate, distribute malware, unlawfully collect personal information, manipulate reviews, duplicate ticket codes, circumvent payment controls or interfere with the platform. Do not use automated scraping or access systems without permission. Report suspicious activity through our support contact.
Tickets, prices and platform fees

Organisers set ticket prices subject to applicable law and their agreement with HIT KENYA. The proposed standard commission is [X]% of eligible sales, with no monthly fees for standard ticketing [CONFIRM FEE MODEL AND COMMISSION BASIS]. Any separate service charges, taxes, payment fees or special commercial arrangements must be disclosed before agreement. The total payable amount and material ticket restrictions must be shown before checkout. Free events and other special arrangements are subject to the applicable disclosed terms.

A ticket is confirmed only when the authorised payment or registration system issues confirmation. A WhatsApp enquiry is not a confirmed booking or payment.
Payments and settlements

Prices are in Kenyan shillings (KES) unless clearly stated otherwise. Where enabled, payment methods may include M-Pesa, cards or other approved payment providers [CONFIRM ACTIVE PAYMENT PROVIDERS]. Never send a PIN, one-time password or full card security details to HIT KENYA support. Organiser settlements, tax obligations, deductions and payment schedules must follow the agreed commercial terms and applicable law [SETTLEMENT SCHEDULE]. Payment provider terms may also apply.
Organiser responsibilities and safety

Organisers are responsible for accurate event details, venue permissions, capacity management, accessibility information, security, emergency planning, required licences, insurance where appropriate, lawful promotions and compliance with applicable national and county requirements. They must honour ticket terms, communicate changes promptly and cooperate in resolving complaints and refunds. Partners must similarly obtain any required licences and meet the relevant service and safety requirements.
Our intermediary role

For independent third-party listings, HIT KENYA provides discovery, listing, communication and, where enabled, ticketing and payment facilitation. The named organiser or provider is responsible for delivering the event or service. Where HIT KENYA itself supplies an event or service, it is responsible for its own obligations as supplier. Nothing here excludes responsibility imposed on HIT KENYA by law, including for its own conduct or representations.
Cancellations and changes

Organisers must inform HIT KENYA and affected customers promptly about cancellation, postponement, relocation or significant changes, and explain available remedies. The Refund Policy sets out the request process. Material changes may give customers refund or other rights under applicable law; no event-level condition removes those rights.
Intellectual property and user content

HIT KENYA branding, site design and original content are protected by applicable intellectual property law. Third-party content remains owned by its respective rights holders. You retain ownership of content you lawfully upload and grant HIT KENYA a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to host, display and reasonably promote that content for operating your listing or requested service. The licence ends when the content is removed, subject to necessary backups, legal obligations and previously authorised materials. You warrant that you have permission to share the content and any necessary releases.
Liability and indemnity

To the extent permitted by law, HIT KENYA is not responsible for losses solely caused by independent organisers or providers, unauthorised resale, or events beyond its reasonable control. We do not exclude liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, our own negligence where liability cannot lawfully be excluded, or mandatory consumer rights. Any limitation applies only to the extent enforceable.

Business users are responsible for reasonable losses arising from their own unlawful conduct, material breach or infringement of third-party rights, to the extent they caused those losses. This does not require a customer to indemnify HIT KENYA for its own wrongdoing.
Suspension and closure

We may restrict or suspend accounts or listings for credible safety, security, legal or material contractual concerns, using proportionate measures. Where practicable and lawful, we will explain the reason and offer a review opportunity. Closing an account does not cancel outstanding payment, refund, dispute or legal obligations. Personal data is handled under the Privacy Policy.
Disputes and governing law

Contact our support team first so we can try to resolve a complaint. Where appropriate, the parties may agree to mediation or another lawful dispute-resolution process. You retain access to competent courts and relevant regulators, including consumer protection authorities. These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Kenya.
Changes and contact

We will publish revised terms with an updated effective date and give appropriate notice of material changes. Changes will not retrospectively remove accrued rights. For questions, contact [LEGAL ENTITY NAME] at [ADDRESS], [EMAIL] or the HIT KENYA WhatsApp contact shown below.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: Understand what information HIT KENYA handles, why it is needed, how to exercise your privacy rights and where to raise a concern.
sections: Who is responsible for your data?

[LEGAL ENTITY NAME], trading as HIT KENYA, at [ADDRESS], is responsible for the processing described in this notice where it determines the purpose and means of processing. For event or service fulfilment, an independent organiser or provider may also act as a separate controller. ODPC registration: [ADD ODPC REGISTRATION]. Privacy contact: [EMAIL]; data protection contact or officer, if applicable: [DATA PROTECTION CONTACT].

This notice is intended to reflect the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019 and applicable regulations. It covers current website interactions and describes additional account, payment and check-in processing only where those features are activated.
Information we collect

• Account and contact information: name, email, phone, role, organisation and registration enquiries.
  • Listings and requests: event, vendor, venue, tour, vehicle or accommodation details and messages you submit.
  • Transactions: where integrated, order details, amount, payment method and transaction references. Full card credentials and M-Pesa PINs should be entered only in an authorised provider interface, never in our enquiry forms.
  • Event entry: where enabled, ticket identifiers, QR validation results and check-in times.
  • Technical data: IP address, browser and device information, security logs and, with analytics consent, usage and visit information.
  • Local browser data: saved marketplace listings, reviews you enter on this device, display theme and cookie preferences. Local reviews are not automatically published to other visitors.

Some current registration screens include identity-document fields. Do not submit ID copies or face-verification photographs until a secure verification process and dedicated notice are provided. If introduced, verification must have a defined lawful basis, limited access, appropriate safeguards and a documented retention period [VERIFICATION PROCESS]. We do not claim biometric matching is currently available.
Purposes and lawful bases

We process necessary information to respond to requests, manage contractual or pre-contractual steps, facilitate ticketing and listings, provide support and fulfil transactions. We may rely on legal obligations for accounting, tax and lawful regulatory requests; on legitimate interests for proportionate fraud prevention, security and service improvement where these do not override your rights; and on consent for optional analytics and marketing where required. Consent can be withdrawn without affecting lawful processing before withdrawal. We will not repurpose personal data incompatibly without a lawful basis and appropriate notice.
Who receives information

We may share necessary information with the relevant organiser or provider for fulfilment, approved payment processors for transactions, hosting or technical service providers, and Google Analytics only after analytics consent on the homepage. WhatsApp enquiries are sent by you through WhatsApp when you press Send; its own privacy terms apply. We may disclose information to competent authorities when legally required or to protect lawful rights. Sharing must be proportionate to its purpose. [CONFIRM PROCESSOR LIST AND CONTRACTUAL SAFEGUARDS]. We do not authorise recipients to use attendee information for unrelated marketing without a lawful basis.
Retention and deletion

We retain information only as long as necessary for its purpose, legal obligations, security and legitimate dispute resolution. Confirm the operational retention schedule before enabling server-side collection: [ACCOUNT RETENTION], [TRANSACTION RETENTION], [CHECK-IN RETENTION], [SUPPORT RETENTION] and [VERIFICATION RETENTION]. The consent choice is retained in browser storage for 180 days before renewal; local reviews, saved listings and display settings persist until removed or cleared by the user. You can clear local data through browser settings.
Security and incidents

We aim to apply proportionate technical and organisational safeguards including restricted access, secure transmission, data minimisation and appropriate processor controls. No online service is completely risk-free. Where a qualifying breach occurs, we will notify the ODPC and affected persons within the time and circumstances required by law. The current static website does not provide secure server-side identity verification or persistent account infrastructure. Do not upload sensitive documents to an unapproved channel.
Your rights

Under Kenyan data protection law, you may be informed about processing, request access to your information, request correction of inaccuracies, object to processing, and request deletion of false or misleading data or erasure where applicable. You may also request restriction and portability where the law provides, withdraw consent, and exercise safeguards concerning solely automated decisions with significant effects. These rights are subject to applicable legal conditions and exceptions.

Send a request to [EMAIL] or use our contact link. We may verify your identity proportionately before disclosing information. We will respond within the applicable statutory timeframe. You may also clear device-local information yourself through browser settings.
Children's information

Independent registration is intended for adults aged 18 or older. Where a child participates in a family event or service, processing of a child's personal data must satisfy applicable parental or guardian consent requirements and protect the child's best interests. If you believe a child has submitted information without appropriate authorisation, contact us so we can assess and take appropriate action.
International transfers

Some infrastructure or third-party services may process information outside Kenya. Where such transfers occur, we must establish a valid legal basis and the safeguards required by Kenyan law. Sensitive data transfers require the applicable additional protections. [CONFIRM HOSTING LOCATIONS, RECIPIENTS AND TRANSFER SAFEGUARDS].
Cookies, external services and communications

See the Cookie Policy for browser storage and analytics controls. We use optional analytics only with consent on pages that load the integration. External photos, links, Google Fonts and communication platforms may involve separate third-party requests or processing; they are not controlled by the analytics preference. Marketing communications must follow applicable consent and opt-out requirements. You may unsubscribe or contact us to stop marketing.
Complaints and updates

You may contact our privacy team or make a complaint directly to the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) using its official complaint form. We will not require you to waive this right. We will update this policy when our practices change and provide appropriate notice. See the ODPC guidance on data subject rights for more information.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.summary: Choose whether HIT KENYA can use optional analytics. Essential browser storage supports features you request and remembers your choices.
sections: What cookies and browser storage are

Cookies are small pieces of information saved by a website in your browser. Local storage is a related browser technology that can remember information on your device across visits. This policy covers both. HIT KENYA uses necessary storage for requested features and permits optional analytics only after you choose to enable it.
Storage used on this website

The following inventory reflects the supplied website files and the updated consent system. Cookie names and durations can vary by browser, provider and configuration. [CONFIRM HOSTING AND THIRD-PARTY STORAGE AFTER DEPLOYMENT].

Type / namePurposeDuration
Essential · hk_cookie_preferences_v1 (local storage)Remember consent choices and date180 days before renewal; stored until overwritten or cleared
Essential / requested feature · hit_kenya_saved_market (local storage)Save marketplace favourites you selectUntil removed or cleared
Essential / requested feature · hit_kenya_local_community_reviews_v1 (local storage)Keep reviews you enter on your deviceUntil cleared; up to 30 entries
Requested display preference · hk-about-theme (local storage)Remember your selected display themeUntil changed or cleared
Analytics · _ga, _ga_* (Google Analytics, if consented)Distinguish visits and maintain analytics session information on the homepageConfigured for up to 180 days; provider may refresh expiry on visits
Marketing · none configured in this updateNo advertising tracker is connected by the shared consent managerNot applicable
Your consent choices

Accept all permits optional categories; Reject non-essential leaves them off; Manage preferences allows individual choices. Optional preferences and marketing selections are recorded but do not activate any additional service in this release. The homepage's Google Analytics script is not requested until you permit analytics. Rejecting optional categories does not prevent browsing or using essential functionality.
Changing or withdrawing consent

Use Cookie preferences in the footer at any time. If analytics permission is withdrawn, the site disables future analytics collection, attempts to remove accessible analytics cookies and reloads the homepage if necessary. Withdrawal does not erase information already collected by a third party. You can clear cookies and local storage through your browser's privacy settings or block cookies entirely. Clearing necessary storage may remove saved listings, local reviews and consent choices.
Third-party services

Google Analytics is an optional homepage integration. Google Fonts, externally hosted images, hosting infrastructure, linked Instagram, YouTube and WhatsApp services may process information according to their own policies when resources load or you follow links. The consent manager controls the identified analytics integration, not every third-party resource or independently operated destination. We will update this inventory if additional tracking or embedded media is introduced.
Updates and contact
We will review this notice when storage technologies or processing purposes change. Contact [LEGAL ENTITY NAME] at [EMAIL] with questions, or review our Privacy Policy.

refunds.title: Refund Policy
refunds.summary: Know when a ticket may be refunded, what happens if an event changes and how to request assistance from HIT KENYA.
sections: Who handles refunds?

For independent events, the organiser sets event-specific refund conditions, subject to Kenyan law and the disclosed purchase terms. HIT KENYA facilitates eligible refunds for transactions processed through its authorised payment system when available. For direct organiser payments, the organiser or payment recipient may need to issue the refund. If HIT KENYA is the supplier, it handles its own refund obligations. A WhatsApp enquiry is not a completed refund request until sent and received.
When a refund may be due

Refund eligibility may arise when an event is cancelled, a significant change affects the agreed service, a duplicate or incorrect charge occurs, the supplier fails to deliver, or the law or published event conditions provide a remedy. We will consider the circumstances and available evidence. Mandatory consumer rights under the Consumer Protection Act, 2012 and other applicable laws take precedence over restrictions in event-level terms.
Cancelled events

If an event is cancelled without delivery, the organiser should notify attendees and arrange any refunds due. HIT KENYA will coordinate the process for purchases made through its enabled payment facilities. Eligible refunds should include the amounts required under law and the purchase terms. A voucher or credit may be offered as an option but will not replace a legally required monetary refund without valid agreement.
Postponed, rescheduled or materially changed events

Where the date, venue or other material element changes, organisers must explain whether tickets remain valid and how customers may seek a remedy. Attendees may choose to retain their tickets if acceptable. If the change creates a refund entitlement under applicable law or disclosed terms, the organiser and HIT KENYA will facilitate it. The notification should specify any applicable response deadline [EVENT CHANGE REQUEST WINDOW], without restricting statutory rights.
Situations where refunds may not be available

Subject to mandatory consumer protections and event-specific terms, a change of mind, failure to attend, arrival after disclosed entry cut-offs, or refusal of entry due to a lawful and clearly disclosed restriction may not qualify. Unauthorised resale, lost tickets or a used ticket are assessed on their facts. These exclusions do not apply where a supplier breach, unfair practice, statutory cancellation right or another legal entitlement requires a remedy.
Platform fees and service charges

Any booking, payment or platform fees must be disclosed before purchase. [CONFIRM FEE REFUND RULE]. Where law requires repayment of the full amount, fees cannot be retained simply because they are described as non-refundable. Any permitted deduction must be transparent, contractually applicable and lawful.
How to request a refund

1. Contact HIT KENYA via [EMAIL] or the WhatsApp contact below, or use the official organiser contact shown on your booking.
  2. Provide your booking reference, event name, purchase date, amount and a brief reason for the request.
  3. Provide only necessary supporting evidence. Never share a PIN, OTP, complete card number or identity document through an ordinary refund message.
  4. We will assess the request, contact the responsible organiser or payment provider as needed and communicate the outcome and next steps.

Request window: [REFUND REQUEST WINDOW]. This administrative window does not remove statutory cancellation or refund rights.
Processing times and payment methods

Once approved, refunds should generally return to the original payment method where possible. M-Pesa: [CONFIRMED M-PESA PROCESSING TIME]. Card payments: [CONFIRMED CARD PROCESSING TIME]. Other methods: [CONFIRMED PROCESSING TIME]. These are operational estimates to be confirmed with the payment providers; any mandatory legal deadlines take precedence. We will communicate material delays and the reason where available.
Ticket transfers and chargebacks

Tickets may be transferred only where the organiser permits it and the official transfer process is available. Do not share a ticket QR code publicly or sell tickets through unauthorised channels. If you believe a charge is incorrect or unauthorised, contact us and your payment provider promptly. You may exercise lawful chargeback or dispute rights; duplicate recoveries are not permitted. We will cooperate with valid investigations.
Complaints and contact

If a refund is refused or delayed, ask for an explanation and review. You may pursue appropriate remedies through relevant consumer authorities, payment providers or competent courts. Contact [LEGAL ENTITY NAME], [ADDRESS], [EMAIL] or our WhatsApp support. See the Terms of Service for other applicable conditions.
